keywords.rule: Counts are papers whose title or abstract contains one of the keyword's phrases (porter-stemmed, as the theme trends); the baseline is the papers in scope first submitted in the 12 weeks before the issue, its own papers excluded. new: fewer than 5 baseline papers; rising: at least 5 papers and a rate at least 1.5 times the baseline rate; hot: at least 15 papers (and 1% of the issue) at a rate at least 0.67 times the baseline rate; steady: otherwise.
keywords.score: log2(1 + n) · log2(1 + (n + 3) / (E + 3)), E = issue papers × (baseline papers with the phrase + 0.5) / baseline papers

themes.name: AI safety, privacy, and robustness
themes.summary: The papers examine safety, privacy, and robustness threats across federated learning, LLM agents, deepfakes, and vision-language models. Some propose defenses such as robust aggregation, encrypted fine-tuning, guardrails, and adversarial perturbations, while others benchmark vulnerabilities like backdoors, poisoning, and quantized-model degradation. They differ in whether they offer certification and governance tools or diagnostic evaluations of attacks and privacy leakage.

themes.name: Robot world models and manipulation
themes.summary: These works build world models, vision-language-action policies, and benchmarks for robot manipulation and embodied control. Several papers improve planning and prediction in latent or video world models, while others target tactile and force grounding, memory, and uncertainty for policy execution. They differ by focusing on model architecture, data and pretraining, or evaluation of manipulation robustness.

themes.name: Visual generation and 3D scene representation
themes.summary: The papers address visual generation, reconstruction, and three-dimensional scene understanding from images, video, and point clouds. Topics include diffusion-based generation and editing, Gaussian and splat reconstruction, point cloud processing, and tracking. They differ in whether they emphasize generative synthesis, geometric reconstruction, or evaluation of scene accuracy.

themes.name: LLM evaluation and reasoning
themes.summary: These papers evaluate and diagnose large language model reasoning, judging, and reliability. They probe chain-of-thought faithfulness, judge bias, hallucination, arithmetic scaling, and benchmark validity across many tasks. They differ in whether they propose new benchmarks, auditing methods, or training techniques to improve reasoning.

themes.name: Efficient LLM inference and architectures
themes.summary: The papers focus on making language model inference and training more efficient through architecture, quantization, distillation, and decoding changes. Topics include linear attention, low-rank adapters, speculative decoding, token pruning, and KV cache management. They differ in whether they target training, serving, or hardware-specific deployment.

themes.name: LLM agents and tool use
themes.summary: The papers study LLM agents that call tools, use search, and coordinate across multiple models or roles. They cover tool-calling data, harness evolution, runtime governance, provenance, and self-improvement across episodes. They differ in whether they contribute datasets, benchmarks, or runtime frameworks for monitoring and recovering agent behavior.

themes.name: Medical and clinical AI
themes.summary: The papers apply AI to clinical imaging, pathology, physiological signals, and agentic workflows, spanning segmentation, generation, diagnosis, and evaluation. They differ in whether they build predictive models, audit benchmarks and documentation bias, or deploy safe review and triage mechanisms.

themes.name: Robot motion planning and control
themes.summary: The papers address motion planning and control for robots, vehicles, aerial platforms, and navigation agents, using sampling, learning, diffusion, and simulation-based testing. They differ in whether they focus on planner geometry, robust control under disturbances, execution and recovery, or language-guided navigation.

themes.name: Optimization and learning theory
themes.summary: The papers study optimization and learning theory across loss landscapes, generalization, spectral estimation, regret, and training dynamics, with applications to scheduling, power systems, and transport. They differ in their mathematical abstractions and whether they provide theory, algorithms, or neural-network verification.

themes.name: Human pose, motion, and tactile sensing
themes.summary: The papers recover human or humanoid pose, motion, and gesture from images, point clouds, EMG, EEG, and tactile or force signals, and they build body models and interaction policies. They differ in sensing modality, target body representation, and whether the goal is kinematic estimation, contact sensing, or embodied human-robot interaction.

themes.name: Mechanistic interpretability and model editing
themes.summary: The papers analyze and edit model internals through causal abstractions, weight-space programming, activation steering, and model merging. They differ in whether they diagnose representations, transfer or merge updates, or intervene on neurons and capabilities for editing and adaptation.

themes.name: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards
themes.summary: The papers develop reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards for reasoning and agentic tasks, focusing on credit assignment, reward fidelity, token weighting, sampler drift, and training efficiency. They differ in whether they introduce process rewards, token-level corrections, system-level rollout methods, or update-geometry adaptations.

highlights.title: Reinforcement Learning Unlearns Corrupted SFT Reasoning
highlights.authors: Anika Misra, Shreyas Vinod, Huteng Dai
highlights.why: Shows RL post-training can recover reasoning after severely corrupted SFT, indicating a surprising robustness and asymmetry in post-training.
highlights.key_result: The paper shows that GRPO post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels ( 60%) even as aggregated SFT-only performance deteriorates under corruption from 43.61% to 13.80%. Crucially, initializing RL with as few as N=8 minimal, incorrect, three-line ``form-only'' traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%, outperforming standard gold SFT initialization (60.71%) and GRPO without SFT (35.00%).
evidence: While aggregated SFT-only performance steadily deteriorates under corruption (dropping from 43.61% to 13.80%), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels ( 60%). Crucially, initializing RL with as few as N=8 minimal, incorrect, three-line ``form-only'' traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%, outperforming standard gold SFT initialization (60.71%) and GRPO without SFT (35.00%).

highlights.authors: Kaustubh Ponkshe, Gyung Hyun Je, Stefan Taga et al.
highlights.why: Proposes search-native pretraining that teaches LMs to use search during pretraining and shows persistent advantages over post-training-only approaches.

highlights.why: Demonstrates weight-space programming can write in-context learning into weights and match fine-tuning, a striking alternative to gradient adaptation.

highlights.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models
highlights.authors: Jiajun Fan, Qinglong Zheng, Ziwen Wang et al.
highlights.why: Shows decision models can serve as zero-shot general-purpose process reward models, significantly improving RL for agents without step labels.
highlights.key_result: We introduce DM-PRM, which turns a general-purpose decision model -- one answering yes/no questions with probabilities -- into a general-purpose process reward model (PRM), zero-shot: no step labels, no fine-tuning, no critic. With Qwen2.5-1.5B it lifts GRPO by over twenty points on ALFWorld and over ten on WebShop, overtakes GiGPO on ALFWorld and learns in far fewer iterations; it also improves GiGPO and GraphGPO on both benchmarks and reaches the highest success of our comparison, ahead of critic-based PPO and of state-of-the-art GiGPO, HGPO and GraphGPO.

It plugs into any policy-gradient method; one model, with one question text per environment, serves household tasks, web shopping and multiple RL methods. highlights.authors: Antoine Lejay, Lionel Lenotre ), Sa{id Toubra

highlights.authors: Hrishikesh Viswanath, Anindita Ghosh, Uttaran Bhattacharya et al.

news.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
news.summary: OpenAI Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki argues for adopting perplexity (cross-entropy loss) as a shared metric across model developers and publishes OpenAI's internal pretraining perplexity measurements, citing log-perplexity of ~0.99 for GPT-3.5, ~0.91 for GPT-4, and current losses below 0.8 where capabilities in cybersecurity and mathematics emerged.

news.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
news.summary: OpenAI describes its approach to detecting and disrupting adversarial distillation, combining adversarial testing, model training, classifiers, API-level protections, and investigations, with a focus on preventing extraction of protected chain-of-thought reasoning. In an internal adaptive evaluation with automated red-teaming, the average attack success rate fell from 54.0% against GPT-6 Astra with original safeguards to 0.2% against GPT-6.2 Astra with updated safeguards.

news.title: How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini
news.summary: Google Research recounts the architectural evolution of Duplex, introduced in 2018, from closed-domain recurrent neural network models to a unified Gemini-based stack, and announces its launch in Tasks in Gemini for calling businesses on users' behalf. The post notes business information from Duplex calls has been shown in Search and Maps over one trillion times, and that Pixel Call Assist features rolled out across five consecutive Pixel generations starting in 2019.

news.title: Meta ads is now available in AWS Quick
news.summary: AWS Quick added a Meta ads AI connector giving Quick access to ads Model Context Protocol (MCP) server operations, so Meta ads customers can create, manage, and analyze campaigns in natural language. The demo shows prompts producing an eight-slide launch-plan deck and a dashboard comparing spend, leads, and cost per lead for two ad sets.

news.title: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together
news.summary: AWS Quick released updates including flows built and refined through chat with deterministic steps and longer-running workflows, an updated web app with a daily briefing that keeps work running after the tab closes, multi-agent orchestration combining several specialized agents into one response, and connectors to Meta ads and Amplitude. The release adds skills on web, configurable content safety and sensitive-information controls, and support for Japanese, German, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), and Vietnamese.

news.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill
news.summary: AWS describes a distributed KV caching skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS that guides coding agents through fit checks, sizing, setup, and troubleshooting of KV caching with Amazon ElastiCache, working with Kiro, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, and other agents supporting Agent Skills. The post states distributed KV caching can cut self-hosted LLM inference costs by up to 40% and time to first token by up to 80%.

news.title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm launched cluster extensions, adding managed extensions for observability and user management to the sixth configuration layer covering software on running nodes, while retaining full node access including the controller node. The post recaps 2026 features including API-driven Slurm configuration, AMI-based configuration, continuous provisioning, automatic topology management with partition-level tree or block topology on Slurm 25.11 or later, and deep health checks testing GPUs and NCCL connectivity.

highlights.title: Reinforcement Learning Unlearns Corrupted SFT Reasoning
highlights.authors: Anika Misra, Shreyas Vinod, Huteng Dai
highlights.why: 表明 RL 后训练可以在严重损坏的 SFT 之后恢复推理能力，揭示出后训练中令人惊讶的鲁棒性与不对称性。
highlights.key_result: 论文表明，GRPO 后训练能一致地将模型准确率恢复到 gold 基线水平（60%），即使聚合的仅 SFT 性能在损坏下从 43.61% 恶化到 13.80%。关键的是，用少至 N=8 条极简、错误、三行的“仅形式”轨迹初始化 RL，可将后 RL 性能提升到 69.30%，优于标准 gold SFT 初始化（60.71%）和无 SFT 的 GRPO（35.00%）。
evidence: While aggregated SFT-only performance steadily deteriorates under corruption (dropping from 43.61% to 13.80%), Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training consistently restores model accuracy back to gold-baseline levels ( 60%). Crucially, initializing RL with as few as N=8 minimal, incorrect, three-line ``form-only'' traces boosts post-RL performance to 69.30%, outperforming standard gold SFT initialization (60.71%) and GRPO without SFT (35.00%).

highlights.title: Search From the Start: Search-Native Pretraining for Language Models
highlights.authors: Kaustubh Ponkshe, Gyung Hyun Je, Stefan Taga et al.
highlights.why: 提出搜索原生预训练，在预训练期间教语言模型使用搜索，并展示其相对于仅后训练方法的持续优势。
highlights.key_result: 在 Wikipedia 和 DCLM-Edu 语料库以及 360M 到 3.3B 参数规模上，搜索预训练模型（ ）在知识密集型任务上表现出更好的性能，并且对检索到的证据具有更高的可引导性。在所有实验中，我们发现 1.4B 模型在所有知识密集型任务上始终优于或匹敌 FLOP 匹配的 3.3B 基线模型。
evidence: Across Wikipedia and DCLM-Edu corpora and 360M to 3.3B parameter scales, search-pretrained models ( ) show improved performance on knowledge-intensive tasks and higher steerability toward the retrieved evidence. Crucially, their advantage persists after supervised fine-tuning of both search-pretrained and conventionally pretrained models, indicating that the tested post-training procedures do not fully recover the capabilities developed during pretraining. Throughout our experiments, we find that a 1.4B consistently beats or matches the performance of a FLOP-matched 3.3B baseline model across all knowledge intensive tasks.

highlights.title: Weight-Space Programming Writes In-Context Learning and Matches Fine-Tuning in Language Models

highlights.title: Large Reported CHB-MIT Adaptation Gains Disappear with Pretrained Encoders and Matched Probes
highlights.authors: Joseph Sankoorikal Johny, Antony J. Sankoorikal
highlights.why: 提供了仔细的证据，表明所报道的较大 CHB-MIT 适应增益在预训练编码器和匹配探针条件下消失，从而纠正了一个被夸大的说法。
highlights.key_result: 在预训练初始化和评估模式下编码器输出上的探针条件下，固定配方在 DL split 上的适应增益对 BIOT 为 -0.6 points（95% interval [-3.8, +2.6]），对 CBraMod 为 +0.01（[-0.02, +0.04]），在 five 个种子上平均。
evidence: The release loads pretrained weights for adaptation only when an otherwise unset configuration key is supplied, and its CBraMod probe reads the reconstruction head with dropout active. highlights.title: Decision Models Are General-Purpose Process Reward Models
highlights.authors: Jiajun Fan, Qinglong Zheng, Ziwen Wang et al.
highlights.why: 表明决策模型可以作为零样本通用过程奖励模型，在没有步骤标签的情况下显著改进智能体的 RL。
highlights.key_result: 我们提出 DM-PRM，它将通用决策模型——一个用概率回答是/否问题的模型——转化为通用的过程奖励模型（PRM），零样本：无需步骤标签、无需微调、无需 critic。使用 Qwen2.5-1.5B 时，它在 ALFWorld 上将 GRPO 提升超过 twenty points，在 WebShop 上提升超过 ten，在 ALFWorld 上超越 GiGPO，并且所需迭代次数少得多；它还在两个基准上改进了 GiGPO 和 GraphGPO，并达到我们比较中最高的成功率，领先于基于 critic 的 PPO 以及最先进的 GiGPO、HGPO 和 GraphGPO。
evidence: We introduce DM-PRM, which turns a general-purpose decision model -- one answering yes/no questions with probabilities -- into a general-purpose process reward model (PRM), zero-shot: no step labels, no fine-tuning, no critic. DM-PRM asks one question per step and adds the standardised answers to the advantage. It plugs into any policy-gradient method; one model, with one question text per environment, serves household tasks, web shopping and multiple RL methods. With Qwen2.5-1.5B it lifts GRPO by over twenty points on ALFWorld and over ten on WebShop, overtakes GiGPO on ALFWorld and learns in far fewer iterations; it also improves GiGPO and GraphGPO on both benchmarks and reaches the highest success of our comparison, ahead of critic-based PPO and of state-of-the-art GiGPO, HGPO and GraphGPO.

highlights.authors: Antoine Lejay, Lionel Lenotre ), Sa{id Toubra
highlights.why: 为线性网络损失景观引入了一种关键的 thalweg 全局结构，具有更简单的几何证明和经验梯度下降对齐。

highlights.title: Latent Space Planning with Sequential Monte Carlo
highlights.authors: Hrishikesh Viswanath, Anindita Ghosh, Uttaran Bhattacharya et al.

evidence: On navigation and manipulation tasks with visual and proprioceptive world models, our formulation outperforms gradient-based planners by 29 and 50, sampling-based planners by 35 and MPPI by 7 percentage points in average success rate, while succeeding in fewer iterations than gradient-based planners and within 4% of MPPI.

news.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
news.summary: OpenAI 首席科学家 Jakub Pachocki 主张采用困惑度（交叉熵损失）作为模型开发者之间的共享指标，并公布了 OpenAI 内部预训练困惑度测量值，指出 GPT-3.5 的对数困惑度约为 ~0.99，GPT-4 约为 ~0.91，当前损失低于 0.8，此时网络安全和数学能力开始涌现。

news.title: Combatting adversarial distillation

news.title: How Google Duplex evolved to also call businesses for you in Gemini

news.title: Meta ads is now available in AWS Quick
news.summary: AWS Quick 添加了 Meta 广告 AI 连接器，使 Quick 能够访问广告 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 服务器操作，这样 Meta 广告客户就可以用自然语言创建、管理和分析广告活动。演示展示了提示生成一个 eight-slide 发布计划演示文稿，以及一个比较 two 个广告组的花费、潜在客户和单个潜在客户成本的仪表盘。

news.title: New in AWS Quick: More capable flows, an updated web experience, and agents that work together

news.title: Cut self-hosted LLM cost and latency with the distributed KV caching agent skill

news.title: Introducing managed cluster extensions for observability and user management in Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Slurm
